text:
mike: Heads up — p99 token latency from NYC POP jumped ~2x around 10:12 UTC, throughput down ~25%. Not correlated with deploys. :eyes:
anya: I see it on the dashboard too, spikes across model-small and model-medium, but model-large unaffected. Any noisy-host alerts?
rachel: infra-bot flagged high procsteal on host nyc-pop-07 around that time. CPU steal percentages hit 35-45% for the host.
infra-bot: [alert] host nyc-pop-07 procsteal > 30% (10:11 UTC). Auto-mitigation: none configured.
dylan: procsteal -> sounds like a noisy co-scheduled VM/container doing heavy kernel activity. Could be batch jobs or backup. Check dmesg and runqueue.
mike: grabbing quick logs now, pasting snippets:
```
# from nyc-pop-07 /var/log/messages
Mar 10 10:09:58 kernel: INFO: task cron_backup:1234 blocked for more than 120 seconds.
Mar 10 10:10:12 kernel: perf: interrupt took 220000 ns
Mar 10 10:11:07 kernel: watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#3 stuck for 22s
```
anya: also pulled runtime traces — we saw kernel-selector fall back to scalar kernels during the spike (fallback reason: cpu-timeout on vectorized kernel). That increased per-token compute by ~60ms on small models.
rachel: interesting — two contributors: procsteal from noisy host + kernel-selector fallback amplifying latency. Any evidence of KV cache churn?
dylan: yes, kv-cache metrics show hitrate dipped from 92% -> 78% concurrent with procsteal window. Looks like requests delayed long enough that cache entries expired from hot set and evictions increased. Payload: per-request kv miss cost ~12ms extra + recompute overhead.
mike: I ran a quick perf record on a repro container post-incident. Key findings:
```
- high rq-sched latency (avg 8ms -> 60ms)
- many voluntary context switches
- vector kernel timed out waiting on cpu slices, fallback path executed
```
anya: action plan suggestions:
- cordon/migrate affected host (nyc-pop-07) immediately to stop noisy neighbor
- add an emergency policy to avoid kernel-selector fallback for small models for 30s if fallback frequency > X
- tune KV cache TTL to be slightly more conservative under host-level schedule anomalies
- add procsteal alert to oncall runbook with automated live-migrate if >25% for 5m
rachel: +1 on live-migrate. Also add a temporary revert patch: disable vector kernel fallback in the selector for the small-model family until we can adjust the timeout heuristics.
dylan: I've kicked a migration for the host and asked infra to check tenant workloads (backup jobs). infra-bot: migrating instances off nyc-pop-07 -> nyc-pop-03 (ETA 2m).
infra-bot: [info] migration started at 10:26 UTC.
mike: after migration, p99 dropped back to baseline within ~90s, throughput recovered. kv-cache hitrate back to ~91%.
anya: good. Follow-ups:
- postmortem with timeline + perf traces
- kernel-selector: review timeout heuristic and add a grace period to avoid flip-flopping during transient CPU steal
- add procsteal-based routing policy: divert new traffic away from hosts hitting steal > threshold
rachel: I'll own the postmortem and the selector heuristic PR. dylan, can you get infra to identify the tenant that scheduled heavy batch and get them to shift windows?
dylan: on it, opened ticket to infra/scheduling team.
mike: for oncall runbook, add a snippet to run these quick checks:
```
# quick triage
ssh nyc-pop-07
cat /proc/interrupts | sed -n '1,20p'
cat /proc/stat | head -n1
sudo perf top -p $(pidof runtime)
journalctl -u runtime -S "10 minutes ago"
```
anya: great. I'll also add an alert that correlates kernel-selector fallback rate + procsteal to reduce alert noise (only page if both trend together).
rachel: thanks all. marking incident as mitigated. We'll follow up in the postmortem with suggested config changes and a small revert + PR for selector timeout tuning. :white_check_mark:
